headline: Both fronts now marked below delivered: BTC -1.8, ETH -10.8. The front expiry is on the CPI date, and ETH takers net sold 4912 contracts into it

events.name: CPI (Consumer Price Index)

consensus.note: No input supplies a consensus for this release.

prior.note: No input supplies a prior for this release.

events.thesis: The high-importance date in the horizon. The 0-1DTE bucket now describes the 2026-10-14 08:00 expiry, which falls on the CPI date, so treat a front position as possibly spanning CPI. Any expiry from 2026-10-15 on spans it outright, including everything in the 5-12 day bucket. Front implied is already below the last 25h of realised (BTC -1.8, ETH -10.8), so a front short has no vol cushion even before any CPI move.
caveats: The source publishes a date, not a time.

events.name: ETH Deribit expiry 2026-10-14 (daily)

consensus.note: No input supplies a consensus for this exchange expiry.

prior.note: No input supplies a prior for this exchange expiry.

events.thesis: This run's odd line. The front ETH expiry traded 20860 contracts, and takers net sold 3477 calls and 1435 puts (net -4912). The next day, 2026-10-15, traded 11618 with net -3676. Takers supplied front optionality while ETH front implied sat 10.8 below the last 25h of realised. An ETH front buyer is buying from that supply; a seller is competing with it at a mark already under delivered. This expiry falls on the CPI date.
caveats: One ~25h window of taker-side flow: not open interest, not a position.
The source publishes a date, not a time.

consensus.note: No input supplies a consensus for this exchange expiry.

prior.note: No input supplies a prior for this exchange expiry.

events.thesis: The cache's only traded expiry in the 5-12 day bucket; it spans CPI and PPI. Takers net bought 349.5 puts and 142.8 calls (net +492.3) on 1586.5 contracts. The bucket's near-money OI put/call rose 0.39 to 1.69, and its put OI peak is 78000, 6.5% under spot. A BTC put seller in this bucket is still selling into taker demand.
caveats: One ~25h window of taker-side flow: not open interest, not a position.

iv_vs_rv.method: BTC 0-1DTE implied minus realised, computed in code: iv_data.dte0_1 (35.133667) minus deribit_cache.realized_vol_annualised_pct (36.97). POSITIVE means options are marked ABOVE what the market just delivered; NEGATIVE means below. The two operands cross two pipelines: implied is a near-the-money bucket mean from the analytics feed, realised is close-to-close log returns over a 25.0h local window. Treat a front position as possibly spanning CPI, and anything from 2026-10-15 on as spanning it. Front OI concentrations: BTC **81500** put / **84000** call; ETH **2460** put / **2560** call.
*Caveat: the source publishes dates, not times.*

**2. ETH takers are selling the front below realised.** On the 2026-10-14 line they net sold 3477 calls and 1435 puts (net -4912) on 20860 contracts, and 2026-10-15 ran net -3676 on 11618. A front buyer can buy from that supply; a seller competes with it at a mark 10.8 under delivered.
*Caveat: ~25h of taker-side flow, not open interest or a position.*

**3. BTC weekly puts still in demand.** In the 5-12 day bucket, put/call rose 0.39 to **1.69**, the put OI peak is **78000** (6.5% under), and the all-expiry put-buying flow strike moved onto the same strike. The bucket's call OI peak fell 6000 to **84000**, 0.7% from spot. Takers on 2026-10-23 net bought 349.5 puts. A put seller there sells into demand; a call seller there is near the money into CPI.

tier_b_caveats: Every level carries a `method` written by the ANALYTICS FEED ITSELF, describing what was actually computed, and a `method_note` written by this generator describing what the number may be USED for. Both travel with the number. Describe a level in those words, never by what its name suggests - and never by a name the feed no longer publishes.

`feed_display_weight` is the feed's presentation ordering weight. It is NOT a statistical confidence, a probability, or a sample-size measure. Do not present it as one and do not rank levels by it as though it were.

SCOPE IS PART OF THE NUMBER. Each level's `method_note` states the tenor and window it measured: 0-1DTE, 5-12 days, 20-40 days, a residual bucket pooling every other expiry, or a 24h traded-activity window. A level may be cited ONLY for the scope it names. A 0-1DTE measurement cannot support a weekly strike choice, and the residual bucket's tenor is NOT STATED at all - it mixes the current-week expiry with expiries months out, so it may be called neither near-dated nor far-dated, however convenient either would be.

Several levels are OPEN-INTEREST PROXIES, and the feed says so in their `method`: an OI peak is where contracts are held, not a demonstrated price barrier. Do not write that a level will hold, cap, or support price. Likewise the delta-flow levels are FLOW, not open interest, and the premium-weighted strikes are traded activity, not positioning.

The level the feed used to call a "Gamma Wall" is now published as a peak OI IMBALANCE, and the feed's own method says NOT gamma, NOT dealer positioning. There is no computed gamma exposure and no dealer inventory model anywhere in these inputs. Never write that dealers are short or long gamma at any price.

An IV or put/call figure delivered as status:"missing" is MISSING: not zero, not average, not 'around 50'. The feed distinguishes two ways a number can be absent and so does this pipeline - a bucket with no samples (unmeasured) and a bucket with samples whose arithmetic has no answer (undefined). A value the feed reports with sample_count 0 is a fabrication by construction and is refused outright. Conversely a 50% IV or a 0.0 put/call ratio that arrives WITH samples is an ordinary reading and is published as observed - do not treat those particular numbers as suspect.

Put/call ratios are open-interest ratios computed by the analytics feed over a band of at most ten strikes each side of spot, not a whole-book market put/call ratio. The separate Deribit figures in tier_b_chain are TRADED SIZE over a ~25h window and contain no open interest at all. Do not mix the two, and do not describe traded size as open interest or as flow positioning.
The feed's freshness stamp is a PUSH time (when the fetcher uploaded), not an observation time. Treat `observed_age_seconds` as an upper bound on how recent the underlying market observation is.
Where this feed and the locally-derived Deribit trade-cache figures disagree, say so rather than picking one.
